name: Grass tuft
notes: One tuft of pasture grass — the unit a grassland is made of, and the smallest plant the engine carries. A cylinder 0.35 m tall and 0.12 m across at a packing derived the same way as a tree crown: LAI x blade thickness / height = 3.0 x 0.30 mm / 0.35 m = 2.57e-03. Grassland LAI runs lower than forest (~1-4); the blade is thicker than a broadleaf lamina and is taken at 0.30 mm. ★ At altitude nobody instantiates a tuft — the ground answers with `grass`'s albedo, which is itself a measured spectrum. This exists for the metre or two where you can see individual plants, and it is the SAME matter either way (Law IV: the camera changes representation, never existence).
